headline: Revolut data breach exposes Bitcoin transaction records as altcoins slide broadly
summary: A security incident at Revolut — in which customer passport data and Bitcoin transaction histories were leaked via a fake government domain request — rattled crypto markets on Sunday, adding a regulatory edge to an already soft session. Bitcoin slipped 0.84% to $76,628, still below the $81,700 level that on-chain analysts say must be cleared to confirm a new bull run. Altcoins took the harder hit: BNB, Solana, and Ethereum all fell between 2% and 3%, while Zcash led losses at -5.41% as privacy-coin concerns intensified.

winners.name: Rain
winners.catalyst: Rain posted the session's top gain of +1.47% amid a broadly risk-off day for altcoins, likely benefiting from relative safe-haven rotation within micro-cap assets; no specific news catalyst was identified.

losers.name: Zcash
losers.catalyst: Zcash led losses with a -5.41% decline, consistent with broader altcoin selling pressure and heightened regulatory scrutiny of privacy coins; the Revolut KYC and Bitcoin transaction data breach may have amplified concerns around privacy-focused assets attracting regulatory attention.

whyItMoved:
The day's dominant story was a data breach at Revolut, the UK-based fintech with a large crypto user base. The company disclosed that a fraudulent request spoofing a government domain tricked it into handing over customer passport data and Bitcoin transaction histories. That combination — personal identity records tied to specific Bitcoin activity — is the kind of exposure that makes regulators and users uncomfortable in equal measure. It didn't cause a market crash, but it added a layer of unease to an already soft session.

Bitcoin's -0.84% slip kept it well below $81,700, the resistance level that on-chain analytics firm CryptoQuant identified this week as the threshold Bitcoin needs to clear before a sustained bull market can be confirmed. Until that level breaks, the market is in a holding pattern — and Sunday's session did nothing to change that picture.

Altcoins bore the brunt of the selling. BNB fell 2.88%, Ethereum and Solana each dropped 2.25%, and XRP slid 2.17%. Zcash took the steepest hit at -5.41%, with the Revolut breach plausibly amplifying existing regulatory anxiety around privacy-focused coins — assets that already draw scrutiny for their ability to obscure transaction trails. Monero, the other major privacy coin in the top 15, bucked the trend with a +1.08% gain, though no specific catalyst explained the divergence. TRON was the only other asset to hold flat, essentially unchanged at +0.01%.
worthKnowing: Revolut disclosed that customer passport data and Bitcoin transaction histories were leaked after a fraudulent request successfully impersonated a government domain — a reminder that crypto data held by fintech platforms carries regulatory and personal risk beyond the blockchain itself.

Crypto billionaires Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne donated a combined $97 million to Nigel Farage's Reform UK party, one of the largest political donations in UK history and a signal of growing crypto-industry involvement in mainstream electoral politics.
Ripple's stablecoin division outlined a $13 trillion addressable market for its RLUSD stablecoin as a corporate treasury instrument, a significant narrative push even as XRP fell 2.17% on the day.
Bitcoin Suisse announced plans to cut up to half its Swiss workforce, shifting operations abroad — a sign of continued margin pressure across crypto service and custody firms.
